title: The 24-hour rule
body: For flights to or from the US booked at least 7 days out, US DOT rules require airlines to let you cancel for a full refund within 24 hours of booking, or hold the fare for 24 hours. Check the seller's own policy if you book through a third party.

title: Cancelled flight? You can ask for cash
body: If an airline cancels your flight or significantly changes it and you decline the alternative, US DOT rules entitle you to a refund to your original form of payment, not just a voucher.

title: Book direct or through an agent?
body: If something changes, an airline can only fix bookings it made itself. With a travel agent or booking site, changes and refunds usually go through them first. Know who you're dealing with before you pay.

title: How we decide what counts as a deal
body: We compare today's lowest fare on a route with that route's own recent price history, and we only call it a deal when there's enough history to make the comparison fair.

title: Check what the fare includes
body: Cheaper fares often come with limits: no changes, no seat choice, or a fee for carry-on bags. Compare the total after bags and seats, not just the headline price.

title: Add bag fees before you compare
body: A fare that looks $60 cheaper can end up costing more once you add checked bags. Look up the airline's baggage fees for your route first.

title: Check your passport dates
body: Many countries require your passport to be valid for months beyond your travel dates, and some want blank pages. Check the destination's entry rules before you book, not the week you leave.

title: Look up entry requirements early
body: Visa or electronic travel authorization rules vary by passport and destination and can take days to process. Check your government's travel advice for the country a few weeks ahead.

title: Set a target price
body: If you have a route in mind, a price watch alerts you when the fare drops to a number you choose, so you don't have to keep checking.

title: Try flexible dates
body: Fares often differ by day of the week. If you can shift your departure by a day or two, compare nearby dates before you book.

title: Separate tickets aren't protected
body: If you book two flights on separate tickets and the first is delayed, the second airline has no duty to rebook you. Leave generous time, or book one ticket.

title: Connections on one ticket are protected
body: When both flights are on a single ticket and you miss the second because of a delay on the first, the airline generally has to get you to your destination. That protection is the main reason to book connections together.

title: A price is a snapshot
body: Airline fares change quickly and inventory at a given price can run out. When a fare on a route you want looks right, check the total and the rules, then decide.

title: Vouchers can expire
body: If you take an airline credit instead of a refund, check the expiry date and any restrictions before accepting it.

title: Screenshot your confirmation
body: Save your booking reference and a screenshot of the fare rules at purchase. It makes any later change or refund request much easier.

title: Carry-on limits differ by airline
body: Size and weight limits vary between airlines, and low-cost carriers can be strict. Check your airline's limits before you pack.

title: Pay in local currency
body: If a card terminal abroad offers to charge you in your home currency, decline. Choosing the local currency usually gets you a better exchange rate.

title: Check your card's foreign fees
body: Some cards add a fee to every purchase made abroad. Check yours before you go, and consider a card without one for travel.

title: Sort out data before you land
body: Setting up an eSIM or checking your carrier's roaming pricing before you leave saves you from hunting for Wi-Fi at the airport.

title: Arrive early for international flights
body: International departures often need more time for check-in, passport control and security. Follow your airline's recommended arrival time.

title: Book flexible lodging first
body: If you're not sure your dates are final, choose a hotel with free cancellation until you're confident in your flight plans.

title: Buy travel insurance early
body: Some plans only cover certain conditions if you buy soon after your first trip payment. Read when coverage starts and what it excludes.

title: Shoulder seasons can be cheaper
body: Travel just before or after peak season can mean lower fares and smaller crowds. It's a trade-off in weather, so check what to expect.

title: Seat selection can cost extra
body: On many fares, choosing your seat in advance costs money. If you're traveling with someone, check the fee before assuming you'll sit together.

title: Check in online
body: Many airlines let you check in online 24 hours ahead. It saves time at the airport and can help you avoid being bumped from a full flight.

title: Photograph your luggage
body: A quick photo of your bag makes it easier to describe if it goes missing, and helps with a claim.

title: Very short connections are risky
body: Even on one ticket, a tight connection in a large airport can go wrong. Check the minimum connection time and how far apart the gates are.

title: Nearby airports
body: Many large cities have more than one airport. Compare fares to each one, along with the cost and time of getting to your final destination.

title: Tell your bank when you travel
body: Some banks flag foreign purchases as suspicious. A quick note in your bank's app before you leave avoids a blocked card at a bad time.

title: Check both directions
body: Before you pay, confirm the dates, the return airport and the arrival times on both legs. It's an easy place for a mistake.
